description.narrative: When catastrophe strikes or conflict occurs in Lebanon and people are in need of an ambulance it is most likely young volunteers who will turn up to help. The country is in many ways in ruin and when it comes to first aid services like ambulances, it is at this stage up to young volunteers to help. However these young people are themselves challenged in a country where their opportunities are continuously being limited . In a cooperation between Danish Red Cross in Lebanon (DRC Lebanon), Lebanese Red Cross (LRC) and Operation Dagsværk we want to give these young people an opportunity to make a change for themselves in a crisis afflicted country. Therefore, we at Operation Dagsværk want to conduct a preparatory study for our next project in Lebanon. The project will be carried out in Cooperation with Danish Red Cross in Lebanon with the purpose to visit the Lebanese Red Cross and their young volunteers who run the ambulance service across the country. The Danish Red Cross (DRC) and Danish Red Cross Youth (DRCY) will be the Danish intermediates and partners securing the Danish link between OD and LCR. In this pilot study Danish volunteers will visit LCR and the Lebanese youths volunteering as first responders in the ambulance service across the country. The purpose of the study is to investigate the challenges that these volunteers face in a country that is going through exceptionally many difficulties and to bring these stories back to Denmark. Through workshops and frequent visits to the ambulance services, where they will follow the evening and weekend shifts, the Danish and Lebanese youths agree on which stories should be told to the 50 000 students in Denmark who will learn about the project. The pilot project will eventually lead to the annual Action Day in which Danish Pupils in solidarity with the Lebanese volunteers will collect money to improve and better the youth voluntary emergency service in Lebanon .
